nodes.title: account
nodes.summary: The login accounts a file authenticates, each bound to a privilege set
notes: Every verb, including read, needs a session signed in with a [Full Access] account (`permission_denied` otherwise).
Address an account by `name` (case-insensitive) or `id`; results report the stored name.
No read reports a password, hash or token; `hasPassword` says whether the account needs one.

The seeded `[Guest]` account (`builtIn`:true) is listed, but update and delete refuse it (`unsupported_operation`) and only its `id` reaches it. `[Guest]` is refused as a name, in any case (`duplicate_name`).

`privilegeSet` naming [Full Access] is refused on create and update (`unsupported_operation`), so this tool never grants it. For the same reason the file's last enabled, native [Full Access] account that can sign in without choosing a new password cannot be deleted, rebound, disabled or forced to change its password; the refusal names the account and the fix. `filemaker help privilegeSet` covers the built-in sets.

File Options logs in with an account by name. Renaming, deleting or disabling that account, giving it another password or forcing a new one is accepted with a `warnings` entry naming the `update:fileOptions` that fixes it; one later in the same batch counts. Until then every open without `--username` fails. A rename that changes only letter case warns about nothing.
To change the login account's password, send `update:account` first and then `update:fileOptions` with the same password; the other order is refused.
seeAlso: privilegeSet

notes: This file is the protected one and `path` names the file let in, as FileMaker Pro's Authorize... button does. The op writes an `inbound` entry here and an `outbound` entry in the other file.

The other file is opened with this file's own account and password unless `account` is given. Both accounts need [Full Access] and the other file must not be open read-only; either failure refuses the op before anything is written.
A rollback does not undo it: FileMaker saves both files when the authorization is written, and the closing summary lists it under `kept`. Running the batch again is safe.
When this file already holds an entry for the other file and the two halves agree, the op is `ok` with `alreadyAuthorized` true and writes nothing. When they disagree, it writes both halves again.
`result` carries `path` (resolved), `account`, `alreadyAuthorized`, and the `inbound` and `outbound` entries as a describe reports them; a dry run omits the entries.
A half missing after the write is `authorization_incomplete`, naming it; running the op again completes the pairing.
A file on a different host is refused (`authorization_host_mismatch`) when this file's File Access requires all files to be on the same host.
A `delete:authorization` earlier in the same batch is refused alongside this op (`authorization_conflict`).

nodes.title: baseDirectory
nodes.summary: The directories externally-stored container data lives under, recorded in the file header
notes: Nothing in this catalog touches the filesystem. An entry records a string, so creating one makes no directory and deleting one removes nothing from disk. A path naming nowhere is a valid entry.
Paths match exactly, case included, unlike names in other catalogs. A filter's `path` is the exception and ignores case.

A file saved by FileMaker Pro can hold several entries with one path. Naming such a path is `ambiguous`, with the entries in `details.candidates`: send the entry's `id` instead. A container field's `options.container.baseDirectory` naming it is `ambiguous` too: use `baseDirectoryKey`.

nodes.title: baseDirectory path
nodes.summary: what a stored path may hold, and how `relative` follows it
notes: A path is at most 200 characters, counted as UTF-8 code points, and at most 797 bytes as UTF-8. Both are checked: 200 emoji are within the first limit and past the second. The limits apply to a `path` sent as an address too; the rules below apply only to a path being stored.

A folder named `.` or `..` is refused, and so is an empty folder name (`a//b/`, or `/` alone). A name that only holds dots, such as `a..b`, is a name. Folders are split on `/` and `\`, except in a path beginning `/`, which splits on `/` alone.
A `:` is allowed only in a Windows drive prefix such as `C:\`. In a relative path or one beginning `/`, it is refused.

A relative or Windows path also refuses `* ? " < > |`, a folder name that starts or ends with a space, and a folder named CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM0 to COM9 or LPT0 to LPT9 in any case. A relative path may not mix `/` with `\`. A path beginning `/` is not judged for these.
`relative` has to agree with the path: `false` when it begins with `/`, a Windows drive (`C:\`) or `\\`, otherwise `true`. A mismatch is `invalid_field`, saying what to send.

On update, `relative` is judged against the path the entry is left holding. A `newPath` of the other kind than the stored path needs `relative` sent with it, and a `relative` sent alone has to agree with the stored path.
Only what an update stores is judged. An entry already holding a path Pro refuses can still be read, deleted and repointed to a valid path.

Neither verb writes to the file, and `--dry-run` changes nothing for them.

keys.summary: the formula text to run

refusedInputs.reason: it applies to validate:calculation only; evaluating takes no slot. Use validate:calculation to check a field, auto-enter or validation formula
it applies to validate:calculation only. Use validate:calculation with 'references': true on the same text

notes: `result.value` is always a JSON string, even for a number, because FileMaker numbers exceed double precision. `dataType` is `text`, `number`, `date`, `time`, `timestamp` or `container`.

A formula that does not parse is an error line, where `validate` answers `valid:false`. `error.details[0]` carries `token`, `errorBegin` and `errorEnd` as in `validate`; a failure while solving has no position.

A formula that parses can still have no value. `1 / 0` is `evaluate_failed` with `dbError` 15 and `Sqrt ( -1 )` is 14, where FileMaker Pro shows `?` and `validate` says valid. `dbError` tells the causes apart.
There is no current record or field, so a field reference answers `calc_undefined` (1224) and `Self` fails 1225. Check them with `validate`, which takes a `context`.
Functions that need a window, screen, device, record or client fail 1225 (`calc_function_not_supported`) instead of guessing, and still validate. See `filemaker help calculation functions` for which.
Global variables set by one `evaluate` stay set for later ops in the run. Nothing reaches the file.

A formula FileMaker refuses is answered with the name in `errors`, `evaluate_failed` where it has none, and FileMaker's number in `engineCode`. An unknown `context` is `tableOccurrence_not_found`, as in `validate`.
See `filemaker help reference calculations` for how a formula is sent, the Approximate keys and contextKey, and the calc_* errors.

nodes.title: calculation functions
nodes.summary: functions that cannot run here and what the rest answer
notes: Every function here still validates, so a formula that calls one can be stored in a field or a script step. The differences are in what `evaluate` answers.

Fail 1225 (`calc_function_not_supported`), for want of a window, screen, device or client: `ValueListItems`, `WindowNames`, `Location`, `LocationValues`, `RangeBeacons`, and `Get` of `ScreenWidth`, `ScreenHeight`, `ScreenDepth`, `ScreenScaleFactor`, `WindowDesktopWidth`, `WindowDesktopHeight`, `WindowStyle` and `ApplicationVersion`. `Self` fails 1225 too: there is no field for it to belong to.
Fail 1223 (`calc_unimplemented`), because only a FileMaker client with a printer answers it: `Get ( PrinterName )`.

Answer an empty string: `Get` of `DesktopPath`, `DocumentsPath`, `PreferencesPath`, `SystemDrive`, `FileMakerPath`, `TemporaryPath` and `SystemAppearance`. A `Get` about a window, layout, record or script answers what FileMaker answers when none is current.

Answer for this machine: `Get ( SystemVersion )` is the operating system's version and `Get ( ApplicationLanguage )` is `English`. `Get ( Device )` is `1` on a Mac and has `dataType` `text`; it compares and calculates as the number.

Design functions -- `ScriptNames`, `LayoutNames`, `TableNames`, `FieldNames`, `FieldType`, `FieldComment`, `RelationInfo` and the rest -- answer for the file on disk, not for this run's changes. A layout created earlier in the run is listed by `read:layout` at once but not by `LayoutNames ( "" )` until a later run. Use the matching `read:` op to check work in progress.

Leave a design function's file argument empty: only `--file` is open, so `ScriptNames ( "Other" )` answers empty even when `Other` is a registered externalDataSource, and `DatabaseNames` names only `--file`.

Under `--create`, `Get ( FilePath )`, `Get ( FileName )` and `DatabaseNames` answer for the file being made, in a real run and in `--dry-run`. `Get ( FileSize )` is its size so far, so it grows during the run.

notes: An invalid formula is `status:"ok"` with `result.valid:false` and exit 0, so the batch is not rolled back. Branch on `result.valid`, never on `status` alone. `valid:false` also carries `warnings`.

`status:"error"` means the question could not be asked: an unknown `context` (`tableOccurrence_not_found`) or a `calculation` that is empty or only white space (`invalid_field`). Parse-error codes come back in `result.error`, not as the line's error.
`result.for` echoes the slot used, including the default.

`errorBegin` and `errorEnd` are a half-open range in Unicode code points of the text sent, and `token` is the text of that range. All three are left out when the error has no position. An error after the last token runs to the end of the text: `1 + ` is [3,4).
Use `validate` rather than `evaluate` to check a formula about to be stored: it runs nothing, and `Self` and unstored field references cannot be evaluated.

Plug-in functions are known only when their plug-in loads here. `External()` and an unloaded plug-in's functions are `valid:false` with `calc_unknown_function`, even where FileMaker Pro with the plug-in accepts them.

`contextResolved` rides with it and is false only when `context` was omitted and the formula names a field without an occurrence. A fully qualified reference needs no context.

notes: Functions are file-global: no verb takes a `table`, and a body names a field as `Occurrence::Field`.
Function names are unique across the file, ignoring case, wherever the function sits. Folders group them and never scope a name. See `help customFunction folders`.
Parameters are written and read back separated by `;`, and so are a body's separators: `Left ( x , 1 )` reads back `Left ( x ; 1 )`. See `help customFunction parameters`.

A read returns `bodyApproximate` instead of `body` when the body names something this run cannot look up, such as a plug-in function that is not installed or a deleted field. It is not a formula. nodes.summary: Deletes a custom function or folder, refusing one another calculation calls

notes: A function another calculation calls is refused as `in_use`, naming every referent in the message and in `error.details` as `{kind, name, slot, function}`. FileMaker would allow the delete and rewrite each calling calculation to `<Function Missing> ( ... )`, which no longer compiles. There is no override: clear or repoint the callers first.

The check is the scan `search:customFunction` runs, so the two find the same callers. A delete that goes through says in `warnings` what was searched and what this run could not read. A call is read from FileMaker's own parse, so a name with a space or punctuation is guarded like any other, and a zero-argument function called without parentheses is found too.

A formula that does not parse counts as a caller when the function's name appears in it as a word; its referent says it `may call` the function and carries a `reason`. So does a quoted name in a formula that also calls a function resolving names when it runs, such as `Evaluate`: its referent says it names the function as text, and nothing rewrites that text.

A formula that is switched off (a disabled auto-enter or validation calculation, a value list no longer calculated, a menu or record-access formula not in effect) does not block the delete, as in FileMaker Pro. It reads back with `<Function Missing>`, which matters only if it is switched on again. `search` still lists it.
Deleting a folder takes both of its members. See `recursive` for a folder that holds members.

The in-use check covers every function in the subtree before anything is deleted. One referenced function refuses the whole op, with all referents listed, and nothing is deleted. A reference from inside the subtree does not block it.

notes: The copy carries the definition unchanged: parameters, body, `availability` and every comment. Change it with an `update:customFunction` afterwards.
Without `newName` the copy is named by FileMaker's generator: `Initials` becomes `Initials Copy`, then `Initials Copy2`. An explicit `newName` that matches an existing function is `duplicate_name`.

A folder is copied with everything in it, and needs no `recursive`. Every copied member is renamed, not only the outermost, because function names are unique across the file: `newName` names the outermost copy and each member under it takes a derived name from its own source name. A copied folder's name is not checked for uniqueness.

Without `folder` and `position` the copy sits right after the original, after its end for a folder. `folder` alone appends inside that folder, and `position` alone re-indexes within the original's parent.
`result` is the copy's name and id, not the original's.
The copy starts unowned whatever the original was, and `ownerId` stamps it, every member of a copied folder included. It keeps the original's `tags`.
The copy is numbered from FileMaker's counter, one id for each member it makes. A copy that would pass the top of the range on create's `id` row is `ids_exhausted`, and nothing is created.

nodes.title: customFunction folders
nodes.summary: how folders group functions, and how a folder path is read
notes: A folder groups functions and never scopes a name. Function names are unique across the file, ignoring case. Folder names are not checked: two folders at one level, or a folder and a function, may share a name.
A by-name op that matches more than one member is `ambiguous`, with the candidates in `error.details`. Pass `id` to pick one, or `type` to pick the kind.

A `folder` path runs from the top level, folder by folder, separated by "/"; "" is the top level. Repeated, leading and trailing "/" are ignored, so `/Plain/Sub`, `Plain/Sub/` and `Plain//Sub` all name `Plain` > `Sub`.
A folder must already exist: one that does not is `customFunction_not_found`, naming the level that was searched and suggesting whole paths. A path is never created.

A path is `ambiguous` only when more than one chain of folders spells it whole, and `error.details` then lists the candidates. A duplicated name partway along is not enough: `Box/Twin/Deep` reaches the `Deep` in one of two sibling `Twin`s when the other holds none.

A folder's name may not contain "/" when it is created, renamed or copied (`invalid_name`). FileMaker Pro allows it; a folder it named `A/B` keeps its name and is reached by the path a read reports for its members.

A folder takes only `name`, `type`, `folder`, `position`, `tags` and `ownerId` on create, and only `newName`, `tags` and `ownerId` on update. Any other key is `invalid_field`, since a folder has no parameters or body. A describe of one reports `type`, `name`, `id`, `folder`, `position`, any `ownerId` and any `tags`.
A function cannot become a folder or the reverse: `type` is not an update key. Create the shape you want and move things into it.
A folder cannot be moved: that is `unsupported_operation`. Move its functions instead. A `folder` and `position` that restate where it already is are accepted and move nothing.

nodes.title: customFunction parameters
nodes.summary: what a parameter name may be, and how its comments pair up
notes: Each entry is one name, taken as FileMaker Pro's Edit Custom Function takes one typed into it. Spaces it trims from both ends (U+0020, U+00A0, U+3000) are trimmed, and `warnings` says so.

`invalid_field`: an entry that is empty, white space or only a comment; a `;` or `,` in a name, including their full-width and Arabic forms; a `//`, `/*` or `${` that is not closed inside its own entry, as in `["x //note","y"]`; and two entries that are the same name ignoring case and width, as in `["a","A"]`.

`invalid_name`: a name with a comment in it or other white space at either end; an operator or punctuation character such as + - * / ^ & = ≠ < > ≤ ≥ ( ) [ ] " $ } or ::; a leading digit or period; a reserved word such as `last`; another custom function's name; and the function's own name, ignoring case. The refusal offers the name FileMaker reads where it can.

A name the function already stores, sent exactly as a read reports it, is kept as it is and not judged. That includes two names that differ only in width, which FileMaker Pro will save: restate the pair as a read reports it, in that order. Any other repeat is refused.
The body is compiled against the final list. A name in it that is neither a parameter nor `Occurrence::Field` fails as `table_missing`, so change a parameter and its uses in the same op.

`parameterComments` pairs with `parameters` by position and cannot be longer than the list the function ends up with: the one in the same op, else the stored one. Shortening `parameters` needs a shorter `parameterComments` beside it, unless the comments it strands are empty. A read gives one entry per stored comment, and `[]` when none has text.

notes: A key you do not send keeps its stored value.

Sending `parameters` or `body` re-checks the body against the final parameter list, so change a parameter and its uses in the same op: a `parameters`-only update whose body still uses an old name fails and changes nothing. A `newName` alone does not touch the body, and calls follow the rename.
A rename onto another function's name is `duplicate_name`, ignoring case. A case-only rename of the same function is allowed, and so is a rename onto a folder's name.

A rename warns where the old name is left in text. References stored by key follow the rename; text does not, so `warnings` names each place `search` finds still spelling the old name, marks one stored but not in effect, and says to change that text to the new name. The rename is not refused. `--dry-run` warns the same way, and a rename that keeps the name, or changes only its case, warns about nothing. See `filemaker help reference search` for what every search reports and which names are held as text.

`ownerId` is not a change: it re-stamps the originating add-on and must come with at least one change, else the op is `missing_field`. To adopt a function without editing it, send its stored `comment` back beside the `ownerId`.
`comment` and `parameterComments` are kept independently of each other and of `parameters` and `body`.

Changing the number of parameters is allowed, as in FileMaker Pro, and always warned about. A call written for the old count evaluates to `?`, and will not compile if sent back unchanged. `warnings` names each caller `search:customFunction` finds and says what was searched and what this run could not read. The warning comes only with an update that lands. Renaming parameters without changing their number warns about nothing.
`folder` moves the member: without `position` it is appended inside that folder, and `folder:""` moves it to the top level. `position` alone re-orders it within its parent.
A refused update changes nothing, even under `--abort-on-error=false`: a later op in the batch still finds the function by its old name.

`overrideName` and `overrideShortcut` each switch on the value beside them: sending `nameCalculation` or `shortcutKey` turns its override on, and sending the flag beside a non-empty value it gates is refused. A shortcut reads back as stored, and an `updateItems` entry that sends it back unchanged keeps it. A submenu or a separator can report an override its kind cannot carry, left by a kind change made in FileMaker Pro; `updateItems` clears it with `false`.

nodes.title: externalDataSource paths
nodes.summary: what a path list may hold and how it is resolved
notes: `paths` is an ordered list: FileMaker tries the entries in turn and takes the first it can find. One relative `file:` path is the ordinary reference and more than one is a fallback chain. An update replaces the whole list.

Each path of a FileMaker data source is a `file:`, `filemac:`, `filewin:`, `filelinux:` or `fmnet:` path to a file, not ending in `/`, with the type matched without case. A path with no type reads as `file:`. A variable may stand for the whole path (`$$path`, `$path`, `$$path[2]`) or follow a type: `file:$$source/Other.fmp12` is taken and `$$source/Other.fmp12` is refused. A path starting `odbc:` names an ODBC source and the rest is its DSN.
Any other path is refused as `invalid_field`, and so are an empty list and a path holding a line break.

Prefer a relative path such as `file:Other.fmp12`. It is resolved from this file's location, so it holds when the solution is moved or copied. Use `fmnet:/host/Name` only when the target is on a different server, or this file is local and the target is hosted.
`fmnet:` takes one slash. The two-slash form that `--file=` uses is refused as `create_failed`.

A `$$variable` in a path has a value only when passed with `--variable='$$path=file:Other.fmp12'`, which lasts for the run and is not stored. An op that has to open such a source fails without it, naming the variable. A fallback path after the variable is tried next, and `tableId` names a base table without opening anything. A local `$path` cannot be given a value.
Paths are stored decoded: `file:a%20b.fmp12` reads back as `file:a b.fmp12`, and `Other.fmp12` as `file:Other.fmp12`. Send decoded paths.
A `paths` equal to the stored list is accepted even when it holds a path that would be refused as new, so a source written by another tool can still be renamed.

FileMaker refuses the delete as `in_use` when a calculated field, a privilege set's record-access formula or the recalculation graph depends on the field. The referents found are in the message and `details`, from the scanner `search:field` uses. The list is best effort, so `in_use` naming nothing still means in use. A reference stored but not in effect (`inEffect: false`) still refuses: a privilege set row moved off "limited" keeps its formula, as does a switched-off auto-enter calculation and an OnWindowTransaction field with no script. A set also keeps the rows of a deleted table; one refusing from there is named by the set alone, with no `slot`, and a `records.access` preset sent to that set clears them.

Anything else FileMaker does not refuse is left to its own cascade, which rewrites rather than refuses. A custom function whose body named the field is orphaned with no `in_use` and no warning, and its body reads back as `Occurrence::<Field Missing>`, which will not compile if fed back in. A relationship keeps its predicate, now pointing at a field id that is gone. Run `search:field` first.

A delete takes out the privilege-set grants given to what it deletes. Each custom privilege set that gave the member a grant of its own has that grant taken out when the run saves, after the delete itself, so a delete that is refused, or whose save is refused, takes none out. When the privilege sets cannot be opened -- on a hosted file someone else may have them open -- the delete still lands, the grants stay, and `warnings` names the sets that hold them.

notes: The copy carries everything: FileMaker copies the field's stored definition wholesale, so attributes this CLI has no key for come across too, which a `read:field` fed back into a `create:field` cannot do. No data is copied; the new field is empty in every record.

A copy of the primary key carries the mark FileMaker gives a copy instead of the key's own. It reads `primaryKey` true in a table with no other key, as with a `toTable` naming one, and false beside a key, the original included, until that key is gone.

References are not rewritten. A calculation, auto-enter or validation calculation and a summary's summarized field are stored as field keys, not names, and the copy keeps them. Within one table that is what you want, except that a formula referencing the field being copied still references the original. FileMaker Pro's Duplicate behaves the same.

A formula calling a function this machine cannot name, commonly a plug-in function with the plug-in not installed, is carried across as stored rather than re-set, because re-setting would replace the call with `<Function Missing>` for good. Such a formula is not rebased: any field or occurrence it names still names the original's, and `warnings` says so.

The copy is numbered from FileMaker's counter, one id for each member it makes. A copy that would pass the top of the range on create's `id` row is `ids_exhausted`, and nothing is created.

nodes.title: field duplicate toTable
notes: FileMaker Pro has no equivalent of copying into another table. A formula resolves from a table occurrence and the copy would carry the source table's, so each formula (calculation, auto-enter calculation, validation calculation, validation message calculation, display-name calculation, and the location of open container storage) is re-set from the original's text against the destination's occurrence. A formula naming the field being copied names the copy. Where the destination has fields of the same names it works.

A formula that does not compile in the destination, for instance because it reads a field through an occurrence the destination's is not related to, is kept inside `/* */` so the field stops claiming to compute something, and `warnings` names it and says why. If it cannot be commented out because its text holds `/*` or `*/` inside a text constant or a `//` comment, the copy is refused as `duplicate_failed` and nothing is copied.

A summary follows the destination's field with the same id, named in `warnings`; a destination with no such field, or one the summary cannot use, is `duplicate_failed` and nothing is created. A variant average's auxiliary field follows the same way.

An auto-enter lookup does not come across, switched on or off: the copy stores none and `warnings` names the lookup that was dropped, with its source, its context and whether it was switched off. Set it again with `update:field`.
A location the field keeps while it stores securely or in the file, and an empty one, are not copied. The copy takes FileMaker's default location once it is switched to open storage.
A stored calculation keeps its storage where its formula still lets FileMaker store it there. Otherwise the copy is committed unstored and unindexed, and `warnings` says so.

The copy keeps the source field's stored name when the destination has no field by that name, so copying `Status` into `Invoices` gives `Invoices::Status`. Otherwise it takes the usual ` Copy` suffix.

A field of another file is named as this file names it: through an occurrence of its table here, `Invoices_ext::Status`, or by the data source and table, `Data::Invoices::Status`. It is looked up in that file and reported wherever this file uses it, through any of its occurrences of that table. A bare name, and a qualifier that is only the other file's table name, reach this file's own fields alone; the second comes back `notFound` with the spellings that do as `candidates`. When the file cannot be opened the answer is `unavailable`, not `notFound`, and `search:tableOccurrence` on the occurrence still reports what names the table there. A data source that opens this file reaches this file's own table, so a field named through it -- by an occurrence, or as `DataSource::Table::Field` -- is this file's field.
See `filemaker help reference search` for what every search reports and which names are held as text.

semanticChecks: every rule on `filemaker help field options` applies to the field as the update leaves it, judged on the resulting state rather than on the request
an `options` object that is present but sets nothing does not count as a change, so an update carrying only `"options":{}` is refused

`fieldType` `summary` is refused (`invalid_field`) on a field another summary field summarizes, naming that summary, because FileMaker builds no summary of a summary (1220). Point that summary at another field or delete it first; earlier in the same batch is enough. A summary that only weights or groups by the field does not refuse the retype.
notes: An update is a partial edit: only the keys present are written, and everything else on the field survives, including attributes this CLI has no key for. `options`, `summary` and the auto-enter lookup are partial edits of themselves too. The field's id is unchanged, and an `options` FileMaker rejects leaves the field as it was.
A legal `newName` that a formula cannot write bare is applied as given, with a `warnings` entry saying how a formula has to spell it.

A rename warns where the old name is left in text. References stored by key follow the rename; text does not, so `warnings` names each place `search` finds still spelling the old name, marks one stored but not in effect, and says to change that text to the new name. The rename is not refused. `--dry-run` warns the same way, and a rename that keeps the name, or changes only its case, warns about nothing. See `filemaker help reference search` for what every search reports and which names are held as text.

An edit that costs something warns instead of refusing, and `warnings` names each loss with what to send to repair it. Nothing is rewritten, and a field's own read writes back unchanged. The warning kinds:
Validation lost: retyping a number field to a date drops its `strictNumber`, and making a field calculated drops all its validation.

Options put out of reach: retyping a number field to a date drops a serial `autoEnter`, turning a field into a summary drops its `autoEnter`, `global`, `indexing` and `autoIndex`, and retyping a container to text drops its external storage. `indexing` is named only when the field ends up with no index at all.

A relationship joined on the field: retyping the key to a container or a summary leaves an edge FileMaker will not accept back (8203), so `update:relation` sent that relation's own read fails. The relation is left as it is and named by its endpoint pair and id.

Stored calculations that lose storage: making the field global, a summary or an unstored calculation unstores and unindexes every stored calculation of the table that uses it, directly or through another, and making it what it was does not bring them back. Each is named. Nothing sent on the edited field silences this one, since the loss is the other field's: set `stored` false on that calculation first, or send it `stored` true again once nothing it uses is unstored. A calculation's own formula edited into one FileMaker leaves unstored warns the same way, and `stored` false sent with it silences that.

Sort levels, export columns and value lists left in a state their create refuses: fewer `repetitions` than a sort level or export column uses, a summary retyped while a level reorders by it or an export column groups by it, a field turned into a container while a field-based value list draws from it. These are the references `search:field` finds, each named with what to send to repair it. An edit to a field an export groups by is not named: `exportOptions` takes a field of any type there and holds a group to no repetition.

A summary's weight or group field (`auxiliaryField`) retyped into a type the pairing refuses, such as a weighted average by a text field: the summary is named and keeps the field as stored. One the op changes is judged, and refused `invalid_field` where FileMaker refuses it.

To consent to a loss and silence its warning, send the setting off in the same op as the value the field ends up with: `false` or `true` on a flag, `"none"` on the auto-enter `type` or on `indexing`, `""` on the validation `message`, and `null` on the five validation settings that take it. Naming a setting the field cannot keep is still refused.
See `filemaker help reference calculations` for how a formula is sent, the Approximate keys and contextKey, and the calc_* errors.
An example that clears a validation rule: `{"op":"update:field","table":"Contacts","name":"FirstName","options":{"validation":{"maxLength":null}}}`

nodes.title: graphNote
nodes.summary: The notes drawn on FileMaker's relationships graph -- text, a box, its colors and its type
notes: A note is presentation only: it does not affect queries and is independent of the graph's tables, occurrences and relations. Deleting those leaves notes in place; deleting a note never cascades and is never refused.

A note has no name and sending one is refused. Address it by `id` (stable within one file, never reused) or `uuid` (survives a clone, a copy or a template transfer); send one, not both. Both come back from a create and a read. Find a note by its wording with a `filter` on `text`.
create and update return the whole note; delete returns it as it was before removal.
bounds: `left`, `top`, `width` and `height`, all four required; `width` and `height` must be greater than zero.
Colors: "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA", alpha last, with an optional leading "#"; six digits are fully opaque. The same form is returned by a read.
font: a typeface name as `read:font` reports it; `fontSize` is in points, 1 to 500.
tags: strings without a leading "#", spaces or "#"; names beginning `^FMI`, `_FMI_` or `^WA` are refused (`invalid_field`).

notes: A member of the Layouts menu is a layout, a folder or a separator. A folder is a Begin/End pair of members, so it is created, copied and deleted as a pair and cannot be moved. Layout objects, with their keys and what a read reports for each kind, are described by `filemaker help layout layoutObject`; a layout's script triggers by `filemaker help layout scriptTriggers`; an object's styling by `filemaker help layout localStyle`.

A layout always has a theme. Left out, `theme` takes the file's most-used theme. A name the file lacks is installed if it is a built-in this machine can add: the default one, which ships beside this tool's FileMaker engine, and FileMaker Pro's own where Pro is installed, as `create:theme`'s `base` reaches them. A name that is neither in the file nor installable fails, and a custom theme cannot be created here. A built-in added this way comes under the name it ships with, so where one of the file's themes already displays that name the result carries a warning (`help theme create`).
Duplicate layout names are allowed, so the `id` in the result is the reliable address.

`type`:"folder" creates a Begin/End pair of members atomically. `type`:"separator" creates a layout that FileMaker draws as a divider in the Layouts menu, and its name must be "-"; it needs a `tableOccurrence` like any layout.

A `folder` that does not exist is an error, not an auto-create, and the message names the failing path component. A path is `ambiguous` only when more than one chain of folders spells it whole; `folder` on `read:layout` says how a path is read.

A folder's name cannot contain "/", which separates the folders of a `folder` path. A create, a rename or a copy that would give a folder such a name -- by its `newName`, or by the name a copy takes (`A/B Copy`) -- is `invalid_name`, and nothing is written. A folder FileMaker Pro named that way keeps its name, and a path still reaches it (see `folder` on `read`).
A `menuSet` name the file does not have is refused when the write applies it.
See `filemaker help reference ids` for how a member is addressed, the not-found code, and how ids are assigned.

A new member created with an `id` takes over no privilege-set grant. What refers to the member by its id is bound to the new one, but a grant a privilege set still stores for a deleted member with this id is taken out, so the new member starts at each set's [Any New ...] level, like any new one. `warnings` names each set that held a grant at another level, with the update:privilegeSet that grants it again.

A folder occupies two ids in this catalog: the one a read reports for it, and a second, hidden one for the member that closes it. So an id can be refused as taken by a folder you cannot see in any listing; read the ids back to learn which are free. The second id is never the one sent but always FileMaker's counter's next, so a free `id` does not rescue a folder: once the counter reaches the top of the `id` row's range no folder can be created in this catalog, and the refusal is `ids_exhausted`, naming the highest `id` a folder still fits at where one does.
See `filemaker help reference tags` for how a tag list is written and read, and which tags FileMaker reserves.

semanticChecks: `ownerId` is a UUID, bare or grouped 8-4-4-4-12 by hyphens; any other spelling is refused as `invalid_field` before anything is created.
notes: The copy is complete: the stored layout is copied as it is, so everything on it comes across, including what `create:layout` cannot write, such as a chart, local styling, conditional formatting and a button action it would refuse.

Left out, `newName` gives the copy the name FileMaker Pro's Duplicate would: "Contacts" becomes "Contacts Copy", then "Contacts Copy2", with no space before the number. Any `newName` is accepted, the original's name included, since duplicate names are legal; the `id` in the result addresses the copy either way.

Left out, `folder` and `position` put the copy immediately after the original. `folder` alone appends to that folder; `position` alone indexes within the original's own folder; `folder`:"" is the top level.

A folder is copied with everything in it, nested folders and separators included, in order, each nested folder closed with a marker of its own. There is no `recursive` flag. The copy lands after the original's closing marker, and only the outermost copy is renamed: the layouts inside keep their names.

A folder's name cannot contain "/", which separates the folders of a `folder` path. A create, a rename or a copy that would give a folder such a name -- by its `newName`, or by the name a copy takes (`A/B Copy`) -- is `invalid_name`, and nothing is written. A folder FileMaker Pro named that way keeps its name, and a path still reaches it (see `folder` on `read`).
A separator is a layout named "-", and the derived name leaves it alone, so the copy is another divider; an explicit `newName` still renames it.

`objectsDuplicated` is every object the copy carries, at every depth, summed over every layout copied, and `membersDuplicated` is the catalog members created: 1 for a layout, and for a folder its two markers and everything between. `createdObjectIds` is not reported, because a copy keeps the original's object ids, which are scoped to the layout; read the copy back by its `id` to address its objects.
Objects in the copy keep their UUIDs and any add-on stamps they carried, as in FileMaker Pro's Duplicate Layout.
The copy is unowned whatever the original was. `ownerId` stamps it, and every member of a copied folder.
A copy of a layout with no theme gets the file's default theme, with a warning naming the layout; the original is left as it was.
Nothing that referred to the original refers to the copy: a `Go to Layout` step, a button or a portal still names the original.
The copy is numbered from FileMaker's counter, one id for each member it makes. A copy that would pass the top of the range on create's `id` row is `ids_exhausted`, and nothing is created.

notes: `create` takes this list as `objects` and `update` as `addObjects`. An `updateObjects` entry takes most of the same keys, addressed by `id`; its page lists only where it differs. On a create or add, a setting left out takes FileMaker's default; on `updateObjects` it is left unchanged. A key that does not belong to the object's kind is refused, not ignored.

The kinds in `type` are writable. A chart is readable through `read:layout` with `detail` but cannot be created or changed, so an update adds, changes and removes named objects rather than replacing the set.

Containers take their children in `objects`: a `portal` holds fields only, a `tabControl` and a `slideControl` hold their own panels, a `tabPanel` and a `slidePanel` hold anything except another panel of the same sort, a `buttonBar` holds buttons and a `group` holds anything. `objects` on any other kind is refused. A `tabControl`, `slideControl` and `buttonBar` need a non-empty `objects`; a `group` or `portal` may be empty.

Containers nest to any depth: a panel's `objects` can hold a group, a portal or another control with its own `objects`. To put objects in a container that already exists, send an `addObjects` entry whose `parent` is that container's `id`.

`anchors` needs all four sides; left out, an object keeps FileMaker's default of top and left only. `anchors` and the position settings (`locked`, `hideWhenPrinting`, `slideLeft`, `slideUp`, `slideBasedOn`, `resizeEnclosingPart`) apply to every kind. On a tab or slide panel they are stored on its control and apply to every panel of it, which is what Pro shows for a panel. `locked` cascades: locking a group locks everything inside it, a control its panels and a bar its segments. A segment takes only `locked`, which applies to the bar. `slideBasedOn` takes effect when `slideUp` is on and is accepted either way. A read reports `anchors` and all six settings on every object, with a panel's and a segment's being its parent's.

Boolean settings that read as the Inspector's checkbox does, true meaning on, are `showNavigationDots`, `enableSwipeGestures`, `showTitleBar`, `applyVisualSpellChecking`, `quickFind`, `showPlaceholderInFindMode`, `overrideDataFormattingWithValueList` and `resetScrollBarOnExit`, even though the file stores the opposite bit for each. `noContextMenu` true suppresses the shortcut menu.

Field: `label` absent labels the field with its own name, "" means no label and any other string is the label text. A field in a portal gets no automatic label. `objectName` on a field also names its label "<name>.label". `repetition` is the first repetition the object shows.

A field may be named by its id instead of by name; send exactly one of the two. The id is for a field whose occurrence is based in a file this one cannot open -- unreachable, absent, or not authorized -- since a name is looked up in that file's field catalog and an id needs nothing opened. Nothing validates an id: a wrong one writes a reference to a field that may not exist, as `tableId` on create:tableOccurrence does, so prefer the name whenever the file can be reached. A read reports the id in place of the name only when the name will not serve -- it could not be resolved or, where the key takes one whole `Occurrence::Field` string, that string would read two ways -- so a read can always be fed straight back in.

Field behavior: `browseEntry` and `findEntry` take `edit`, `selectOnly` (contents can be selected and copied but not changed), `viewOnly` (the field cannot be entered) or `setByCalculation`, which consults `entryCalculation`; a field in that state with no calculation cannot be entered at all. `exitOnTab`, `exitOnReturn` and `exitOnEnter` are independent. `keyboardType` affects only touch devices and `inputMode` is the input method for Japanese text. A label also takes `quickFind`, searching the fields its merge fields name; it is refused on a label with no merge field naming a searchable field. A read reports `browseEntry`, `findEntry`, `selectContentsOnEntry`, the three exit keys, `applyVisualSpellChecking` and `quickFind` on every field, `inputMode` and `keyboardType` unless the stored value names none of their options, and `quickFind` on a label only where it can be set.

Field data: `control` styles that draw their choices from a value list (drop-down list, pop-up menu, checkbox set, radio button set) need `valueList`; send both in one entry, or switch between two list styles and the field's list is kept. `selectionList` is reported by a read and refused by a write. `repetition` is where the object starts and `repetitionCount` how many it shows from there; a start that would push the span past the field's last repetition is refused, so send both keys to move a span. `repetitionCount` resizes the object and can be refused where the object must stay inside a portal row or a clipping container. `repetitionOrientation` and `repetitionCount` share one stored number, so sending one keeps the other. A read reports all of these on every field whatever its control style, with `repetitionCount` unsigned; `allowEditingOfValueList` on an edit box is stored and inert, not absent.

Graphic format: `graphicSizing`, `maintainOriginalProportions`, `horizontalAlignment` and `verticalAlignment` apply to a container field and to a `graphic`; `optimizeFor`, `autoPlay`, `noContextMenu` and `preservePdfTransparency` apply to a container field only, and a read leaves them off a graphic. Settings Pro greys out are still accepted, for example `maintainOriginalProportions` with `cropToFrame`. A field created here reads `cropToFrame` with proportions false, a field created in Pro reads `reduceToFit` with proportions true, and a `graphic` created here reads `reduceOrEnlargeToFit` with proportions false, so its picture is stretched to fill the object until `maintainOriginalProportions` is set. An alignment is absent in a read only when the stored value names no choice.

Label and button: `text` is required on a `label`, optional on a `button`, and refused on any other kind. A `<<Occurrence::Field>>` in it, or a bare `<<Field>>` of the layout's occurrence, becomes a merge field when it names a field at the time the text is written: it shows the field's value and follows a rename. One naming no field stays characters, and stays so when such a field is created later, until the text is written again; `search` reports it as a possible hit. A read lists merge fields under `mergeFields`, Pro-authored ones included. A button-bar segment's label is a calculation and holds none. `fixedWidth` applies to a label only.

Portal: `tableOccurrence` is the occurrence whose related records it shows, not the layout's own. `initialRow` is 1-based. `allowVerticalScrolling` is the checkbox and `scrollBarVisibility` (`always` or `whenScrolling`) is the picker labelled "Show scroll bar:"; Pro greys the picker out until the checkbox is on, and either is accepted alone. `useAlternateRowState` and `useActiveRowState` are Portal Setup's row checkboxes; styling part `row_alt` or `row_active` in `localStyle` turns the matching one on, with a warning, and `revertLocalStyle` turns either back on if it was off. A read reports `initialRow`, `allowVerticalScrolling`, `scrollBarVisibility`, `allowDelete`, `resetScrollBarOnExit` and both row states on every portal, even `scrollBarVisibility` on one with no bar, and `sort` and `filter` when it has them. The row states are reported here and not in `localStyle`.

Web viewer: a create or add needs exactly one of `url` and `urlCalculation`; an update takes at most one, and neither leaves the address as it is. `url` is a literal address, quoted for you; `urlCalculation` is a formula, which a per-record address needs, and a field in it must be named "Occurrence::Field" because a layout object's calculation has no table context. A formula of only white space is refused, and one FileMaker cannot parse fails the op. Left out, the six settings take: interaction, progress bar, status messages and URL encoding on; Find-mode content and JavaScript-to-scripts off. A web viewer is created with no border on any side. A read reports `type`:"webViewer" with a `webViewer` object holding `urlCalculation` and the six settings, and `urlCalculation` is what an update accepts back. A chart reports `type`:"chart" and nothing more.

Shapes: `line`, `rectangle`, `roundedRectangle` and `oval` have no keys of their own. Their appearance comes from the theme, or from `localStyle` on an update. A `line` runs from its box's top-left corner to its bottom-right; there is no direction key, so a read reports a line's `bounds` and not its endpoints.

Button icon: `icon` is a path to a PNG or SVG file on the machine running the CLI, judged by its extension; the bytes are copied into the file's image library and the path is not stored. "" takes the icon away. `iconSize` is in points, 8 to 128. `iconPosition` says whether the button draws its label, its icon or both, and on which side; `none` shows the label alone and leaves the stored icon. The three keys are independent: choosing a position does not pick an icon, and `none` does not remove one. They apply to a `button`, a `popoverButton` and a button-bar segment, which has one icon of its own. An icon set by a calculation is not visible to this CLI. A read reports `iconId` (the image-library member, absent when there is no icon; not a write address), `iconSize` and `iconPosition` on each of those kinds.

Tab control: `tabWidthStyle`, `tabWidthModifier`, `tabWidthUnits` and `tabsShareSingleStyle` are the stored parts of Tab Control Setup and belong to the tab control; sending one for a panel is refused with the control's id. `tabWidthModifier` is always in points whatever `tabWidthUnits` says: the unit only sets what Pro's dialog displays. Three of the five width styles use the modifier, and a value is accepted and stored for the other two. The tab list is each panel's `title`, the default front tab is `defaultPanel`, and tab justification is styling; the tab position and height are not settings. A read reports the four settings on the control, with `tabWidthUnits` absent when the stored value names no unit. It also reports `visiblePanel` on a tab or slide control and `defaultPanel` on a tab control, each as a panel's `id`; `visiblePanel` cannot be written, and a slide control's default is its first panel.

Panel titles: `title` is the text on a `tabPanel`'s tab, and on `updateObjects` also a popover's heading. It is stored as a literal, quoted into a calculation for you; for a live heading send `titleCalculation` instead. Send at most one, and neither leaves the title alone. A `slidePanel` has no title. A read reports a title calculation under `titleCalculation`.

Slide control: `showNavigationDots` and `enableSwipeGestures` are Slide Control Setup's checkboxes and belong to the control, not a panel. Neither changes the control's geometry: hiding the dots does not reclaim their space. `dotSize` is in whole points and needs `showNavigationDots` on. `padding` takes `top`, `right`, `bottom` and `left` in points on a slide control or a popover. A read reports the two checkboxes on every slide control, and `dotSize` and `padding`, which are worked out from the positions of the parts inside and left out of `localStyle`.

Popover button: it creates two objects, the button and the popover it opens, and both ids come back, the button first; there is no `popover` type. The popover goes in the button's `popover`, with its settings, its `width` and `height`, and its contents in `objects`, and a read reports it there, as Pro's Objects pane shows it. A popover has no position to set: Pro draws it beside its button each time it opens, so `bounds` is refused on it. `popoverArrow` names the popover's own edge that carries the arrow, so the popover opens on the opposite side: `left` puts it to the right of its button. It is a preference: FileMaker tries that edge first and falls back to the others when the popover does not fit. `showTitleBar` false hides the strip along the top and keeps the title. Send `popoverArrow`, `showTitleBar` and `title` for the popover, not for its button. A read reports `popoverArrow` and `showTitleBar` on every popover, and its `title` even when the bar is hidden.

Button bar: its segments are ordinary `button` entries in `objects`, each with its own `text` and `action`; there is no `segment` type. `orientation` is `horizontal` or `vertical`; it re-lays out every segment and leaves the bar's `bounds` alone. Send it for the bar: a segment is refused, with the bar's `id`. `activeSegment` names the current segment by `id`, 0 for none, and a read reports it only when a segment is marked. On a new bar, as with a new tab control's `defaultPanel`, the `id` is the child entry's own.

Calculations: `tooltip`, `hideCondition`, `accessibilityTitle`, `accessibilityHelp`, `placeholderText` and `entryCalculation` hold a calculation as the box in Pro does. Quote a literal (`"Save this record"`), and name a field with its occurrence (`Contacts::Name`). A value that does not parse is refused, naming the quoted form. "" clears it. `applyInFindMode` is the checkbox beside `hideCondition` and does nothing without one; `accessibilityLabel` is the `id` of another object on this layout whose text labels this one, and 0 clears it; on a new object it can name another entry's `id`. On a tab or slide panel `hideCondition` and `applyInFindMode` land on its control. `placeholderText` and `entryCalculation` apply to a field, and `placeholderText` is refused on a checkbox set or radio button set. A read reports each calculation only when the object has one, a value typed as plain text read back quoted (`"Hello there"`), `applyInFindMode` on every object, and `accessibilityLabel` only when it names an object still on the layout.

A read reports `localStyle` on an object that has local styling, in the shape an update takes back; `filemaker help layout localStyle` describes it. A read reports `scriptTriggers` as the object's own triggers, absent on a kind that cannot hold one and `[]` on one that can and has none; a label, shape, graphic, button bar, panel and a group with no action report none. A new object takes its triggers in `scriptTriggers`, an existing one in `setScriptTriggers`. A read reports `tags` with `detail` when the object has any.

`tags` on an object entry is the object's own list and is kept apart from the layout's. On an update the list replaces the current one, `[]` clears it, and leaving it out keeps it. Setting `action` keeps the tags.

nodes.title: layout layoutObject action
notes: Button and group: `action` is the one script step the object performs when clicked, as the step object `read:layout` reports and one line of a script's `body` is; `filemaker help script steps` lists a step's keys. Left out, the object does nothing; `{"stepID":0}` says so explicitly and is what a read reports. A group takes `action` too, because FileMaker makes a group a button by giving it a step. A `popoverButton` takes none. For example `{"type":"button","text":"Go","action":{"stepID":1,"script":"Invoice","parameter":"\"hi\""}}` performs a script and `{"stepID":6,"layout":"Summary"}` goes to a layout. A calculation inside the step is a calculation, so quote a literal string, and a name in it must already be in the file when the op runs: a table or field created by an earlier op in the same stream is not yet visible. Sixteen steps cannot go on a button and are refused naming the step: If, Else, Else If, End If, Loop, Exit Loop If, End Loop, Allow User Abort, Set Error Capture, Set Layout Object Animation, Set Revert Transaction on Error, Set Script Triggers, Open, Commit and Revert Transaction, and the comment step. A read reports `action` on every button and group, and `text` on a button unless it is unlabelled.

notes: `bounds` width and height must be greater than zero; a `line` may have one of them zero. A `tabPanel`, a `slidePanel` and a button-bar segment take no `bounds`: a panel has its control's rectangle and a segment has the bar's divided by the segment count.

notes: This is Pro's Format > Conditional Formatting dialog: an ordered list of conditions, the same on read, `addObjects` and `updateObjects`. A write replaces the whole list, as the dialog's OK does, so to change one condition send back the list a read gave with that one changed; `[]` removes them all. A read reports every condition, switched-off ones included. Fields, text objects, buttons, popover buttons, tab panels, slide panels, web viewers and charts take conditions, as in Pro.

`formula` is the calculation FileMaker evaluates; a field reference names its table occurrence, and `Self` is the object's value. `enabled` defaults to true. `set` is the formatting, in the names and spelling `localStyle` uses; a condition takes the 12 settings of the Text section of the Appearance tab, plus `background-color` and `-fm-icon-color`, and nothing else. The highlight is yellow or none, as in the dialog.

Five settings draw only when ticked: `color`, `background-color`, `font-family`, `font-size` and `-fm-icon-color`. `applied` lists the ticked ones; left out on a write, each of the five that `set` gives is ticked. A read always lists them, so values Pro stored with their box off survive a round trip.

A condition is Pro's "Formula is" when it has `formula`, and its "Value is" when it has `valueIs`: a comparison and the values Pro shows fields for, such as `{"comparison":"containing","first":"Alpha"}`. From `valueIs` the formula is built as Pro's dialog builds it, here `PatternCount(Self; "Alpha") > 0`; a number, date or time value is read in the file's formats. `empty`, `beforeToday`, `today` and `afterToday` take no value, `between` and `notBetween` take `first` and `second`, and the rest take `first`. A read reports both `formula` and `valueIs`, and both may be sent back while `formula` is the built one. Pro's Revert and `revertLocalStyle` leave conditions alone.

notes: Graphic: `picture` is a path on the machine running the CLI, read while the op runs. nodes.title: layout localStyle
nodes.summary: an object's own styling, one entry per part and state

keys.summary: the part, by the engine's name, for example self, icon or inner_border
the state, by the engine's name, for example normal, hover or focus
CSS names and values in FileMaker's spelling; "" removes that setting

notes: Local styling is settings stored on the object itself that replace what its theme style gives it, as Pro's Inspector Appearance tab writes them. A read reports the same entries, so a read value writes back unchanged. `part` and `state` are the engine's names, not the Inspector's labels; `filemaker help reference localStyleParts` lists every part and state for each kind of object with the label Pro shows. Common parts: `self` (the object), `icon` (a button's icon or a field's drop-down icon), `inner_border` (a button's padding and inner shadow), `text` (a field's padding, as margins) and `baseline`. States: `normal`, `hover`, `pressed`, `focus` (In Focus) and `placeholder` (Placeholder Text). A setting is accepted only where the Inspector has a control that writes it, and a refusal names the parts and states that take it.

Values use FileMaker's spelling and are refused rather than guessed: lengths like `4pt` or `0.5em` with no space and no padding zeros; colors as `rgba(100%,0%,0%,1)` with no spaces, or `#RRGGBB`; gradients as `-webkit-gradient(linear,0% 0%,0% 100%, from(<color>), to(<color>))`. A refusal suggests the spelling. A value can read back differently, `#FF0000` as `rgba(100%,0%,0%,1)`: FileMaker stores each channel as a fraction, and colors made in Pro can fall between the 256 steps `#RRGGBB` can say, so send a color back as it was read to keep it exact. A color with transparency takes the `rgba(...)` form; `#RRGGBBAA` is refused.

Shorthands are refused: send `padding-top` and its three siblings, not `padding`. Line width, line color and corner radius each write every side, so a write naming one side must name all four with the same value; a line style may be `none` on a side that is switched off. `""` removes a setting and the part returns to its theme style. There is no `inherit`, because FileMaker inherits by not storing a setting.

Some writes also make others, as the same change in Pro does: a fill color, gradient or image clears the other kinds of fill, a line style switches off the inner border's line, a field's line also sets the line between repetitions, text alignment moves the icon to match, and icon padding is written at every state. Each such change comes back as a warning with the value it replaced, so send that value to undo it. An object from a file converted from FileMaker 11 or earlier can have a legacy engraved, embossed or drop shadow, shown by `-fm-fill-effect` in a read. Any line style removes it, as in Pro, and it cannot be put back; while it stays, a line width or color goes where the effect keeps the line, often `inner_border`, and a warning says so.

`font-family` is a bare name such as `Helvetica Neue`, with no quote marks, or the form a read returns, `-fm-font-family(<family>,<PostScript name>)`. It must be in the file's font list or installed on this computer, otherwise it is refused. A font installed here but new to the file is added, with a warning, since a computer without it shows a substitute.

`background-image` is a new image as `url(<path>)`, a path on the machine running the command, read while the op runs; or an image already in the file, as the value a read gives for it, `-fm-image-data(<name>;data:<type>;LibraryReference, id="<entry>" key="<checksum>")`, sent back unchanged. The file must hold that entry with that checksum. Base64 image data is refused. Choosing an image fill also sets the fill color to none and the image position to `center center`, or `left top` where the part's `background-repeat` is `repeat`, as in Pro.

Image sizing is Pro's Sizing pop-up, sent as the settings a read shows, in FileMaker's spelling, and only as one of its five groups. Original Size is `background-position` `center center`, `background-size` `""` (the empty size Pro stores, not a removal) and `background-repeat` `no-repeat no-repeat`. Scale to Fit and Scale to Fill are the same with `contain` or `cover`. Tile is `background-position` `left top` alone. Slice is `border-image-slice`, four amounts and `fill` such as `20% 20% 20% 20% fill`, with `border-image-width` `auto auto auto auto`, and keeps the image in `border-image-source`. Each choice places the image sent with it, or the one the fill already has, and the other settings it writes come back as warnings. `border-image-slice` alone changes the amounts of a fill already sized as Slice. An image sent onto a sliced fill goes into `border-image-source`, and its amounts start over at 20%, as in Pro.

`revertLocalStyle`: true clears all of the object's local styling, as Pro's Revert does, before any `localStyle` in the same entry, and keeps the named `style`. A locked object is refused, as in Pro; unlock it in the same entry with `locked`: false. A new object takes `localStyle` in its `objects` or `addObjects` entry, but not `revertLocalStyle`.
A popover is styled on the popover, not on its button: part `self` is the title area and `contents` the panel, and a font size on `self` also moves the title and the panel to fit, as in Pro.

A tab control, a slide control and a button bar are each drawn from several objects, and FileMaker stores each setting on one of them. A read shows a setting on that object and a write names that object; a write sent to another is refused, with the object id and part to send it to. The warnings of a write or a revert list any other panels or segments it also changed.

Tab control: text and paragraph settings (font size, color, style, alignment, line spacing, indents, tab stops) are stored on the tab control, once for all its tabs. Fill, line, corner radius, shadows, padding and vertical alignment are stored on each tab panel. So a tab panel that reports no font takes it from its tab control, and a tab control that reports no fill takes it from its panels. A panel's four corners are `-fm-tab-top-left-radius`, `-fm-tab-top-right-radius`, `border-bottom-right-radius` and `border-bottom-left-radius`, sent together like other corners. When the control's `tabsShareSingleStyle` is on, a write to one panel is copied to every panel, except vertical alignment, which stays on the panel named. `revertLocalStyle` on such a panel clears every panel.
Slide control: it stores all its styling itself. Part `self` is the control, `contents` is Pro's Panel part and `dot` is its Dots part. A slide panel stores no styling, and a write to one is refused.

Button bar: part `self` is Pro's Button Bar part and `button_bar_divider` its Dividers. The segments store Pro's Button Bar: Segment and Button Bar: Icon parts, as `self` and `icon`. Pro styles every segment alike, so a write to one segment is copied to every segment and any one can be named; `revertLocalStyle` on a segment clears every segment. On tabs, slide control dots and button bar segments, state `checked` is Pro's Active and `normal` is its Inactive.

A read reports two markers apart from `localStyle`, each only when true, and neither can be written: `keepClassicTheme` means the object keeps the classic theme's look whatever theme the layout uses, and the Inspector then offers the classic list of parts, without a field's Button and Icon parts; `drawsAsText` means an older kind of field that FileMaker draws like a text object. A label's `textAlign` and a web viewer's `border` repeat part of `localStyle` and are deprecated, so read `localStyle` instead.

notes: A describe carries no subtree, folders included: a folder describe reports its id, position and `hidden`, and a listing with `folder` shows what is inside. A describe reports its own `folder`.
Layout names are not unique. A name two members share is `ambiguous`, with the candidates in `error.details`, and `id` picks one.

`type` narrows a duplicated name before it is resolved: a layout named `Dashboard` inside a folder named `Dashboard` is `ambiguous` without it and resolves with it. A name matching only the other kind is `layout_not_found`, with what it did match in `error.details.candidates`.
A describe reports what is stored. Access levels are not reported, because access belongs to the reader and not to the layout.

`detail` reports every object type as a tree under `contents`, not the Data API's two flat lists, so a caller deciding whether an update is safe sees what else is there. `unmodelledCount` is how many objects an update would leave untouched. What a read reports for each kind of object is on `filemaker help layout layoutObject`.

Every object in `contents` carries an `id`, scoped to the layout rather than the file: two layouts of one file both hold an object 1. It survives a commit and a reopen, a deleted object's number is not reused, and it is the address `removeObjects`, `updateObjects` and `duplicateObjects` take.
`geometry.bodyHeight` is the body part's height, absent for a layout with no body part (a header-and-footer-only report layout, for example).
seeAlso: `filemaker help reference forms` — what JSON a key's type, its requiredness and a filter's tag each take

nodes.title: read:layout list
nodes.summary: Every layout and folder in custom display order, nested or flattened, whole catalog or one folder

keys.summary: adds every listed layout's object tree under `contents`, which loads one object store per layout
scopes the listing to one folder's subtree, by "/"-separated path
emits every member at every depth as one flat list, each carrying its `folder` path
narrows the listing to the members matching every attribute given

semanticChecks: a filter needs 'flatten':true. A listing is nested by default, so a filter could only test the top level and would silently drop every match inside a folder.

a tags filter is a non-empty string, or a non-empty array of non-empty strings: a tag is never empty, so an empty pattern matches no tag and the request could only ever come back empty, and an empty array requires nothing, so it would keep every member and narrow nothing.
notes: A listing is a tree by default, and its `total` counts nodes at every depth. A folder carries `items`; a layout never does.

`flatten` returns the same members as one flat array, depth-first, each carrying the `folder` path it sits in: absolute, "/"-separated and "" at the top level, so it feeds straight back into `folder` on create or update. A folder is still reported, without `items`, so `type` tells the kinds apart. A folder whose name holds "/", which FileMaker Pro allows, can make a path `ambiguous` when another chain of folders spells the same path.
`position` is relative to the parent in both modes and is never renumbered across a flattened list, so `folder` plus `position` stays the address an ordering write targets.

`filter` narrows a listing to the members matching every attribute given, and needs `flatten`:true. `total` counts every member the listing covers and `returned` counts what matched, so a filter that matches nothing is an empty `items`, not an error. Filtering by `tableOccurrence` never returns a folder, which has none.
`folder` scopes a listing to one folder's subtree and composes with `flatten`; `total` then counts that subtree. A scope that names no folder is `layout_not_found`.

A `folder` path is matched against the folders the file has, so a folder whose own name holds "/" -- which FileMaker Pro allows -- is reached by the path a read reports for its members: `A/B` names a folder called `A/B` as readily as a `B` inside an `A`. A path is `ambiguous` only when more than one chain of folders spells it whole, and then the candidates are in `error.details` rather than a guess: two sibling folders of one name that both carry the path to its end, or a name holding "/" beside a chain that spells the same path. A duplicated name partway along is not enough -- `Box/Twin/Deep` reaches the `Deep` in one of two sibling `Twin`s when the other holds none. A path that names nothing is read once more with repeated, leading and trailing "/" ignored, so `/Plain/Sub`, `Plain/Sub/` and `Plain//Sub` all name `Plain` > `Sub`; one that still names nothing is not-found, naming the folder that was missing and the one it was looked for in, with suggestions as whole paths.

keys.summary: which layout event fires the script

seeAlso: `filemaker help reference forms` — what JSON a key's type, its requiredness and a filter's tag each take
notes: A layout's own triggers use the twelve layout events listed under `event`. An object event is refused here and is set with `setScriptTriggers` inside an `updateObjects` entry; a file-level event such as OnFirstWindowOpen or OnTimer belongs to no layout and is set through `update:fileOptions`. An unknown event, in `removeScriptTriggers` too, is `unknown_field_type` with the closest names.

Name the script with `script` or `scriptId`, exactly one. It must already be in this file, so put `create:script` earlier in the same stream; a trigger on a script in another file can be read but not written. Two scripts may share a name, and a name several scripts hold is `ambiguous` with their ids, so `scriptId` is then the only address. A read reports `script.id` beside `script.name`, and the name is absent when it could not be resolved: bind that trigger by id.

`modes` holds any of `browse`, `find` and `preview`, matched without regard to case; absent means all three. The modes are where the trigger is enabled, so `[]` is refused. An unknown mode is `unknown_field_type` with the closest names.

`parameter` is a calculation parsed in the layout's table occurrence, so quote a literal: `"parameter": "\"done\""`. An unquoted bare word, and a value of only white space, are refused. Leave it out for none.

A layout holds one trigger per event. On a create, naming an event twice leaves the last. On an update, `setScriptTriggers` upserts by event and `removeScriptTriggers` runs first, so one op can repoint a trigger or narrow its modes; events not named keep their triggers. Removing an event that has no trigger is a warning, not an error, and `triggersRemoved` says how many were removed.
An object's own triggers are set per object: `scriptTriggers` in a new object's entry, `setScriptTriggers` inside an `updateObjects` entry.

refusedInputs.reason: 'type' cannot be changed on an update: a folder is a pair of members, so a layout cannot become one, and a separator is a layout named "-", so rename it.
update:layout has no 'objects', because replacing the set would delete objects this CLI cannot recreate, such as a chart. Use 'addObjects', 'updateObjects', 'duplicateObjects' and 'removeObjects'.

semanticChecks: `addObjects`, `removeObjects`, `updateObjects`, `duplicateObjects`, `setScriptTriggers` and `removeScriptTriggers` must not be empty: an update that changes nothing is a mistake, not a no-op.
a `tags` entry containing a space or a `#` is refused as `invalid_field`.
notes: The object keys run in one order: `removeObjects`, then `updateObjects`, then `duplicateObjects`, then `addObjects`. So one op can replace an object by removing it and adding it back, but an edit or a removal cannot name an object the same op creates. An added object with no `bounds` is placed below the lowest object the earlier keys left on the layout.
Changing `tableOccurrence` leaves the fields already on the layout pointing at their own occurrences, which FileMaker shows as <Table Missing>; a warning says so.
`folder`:"" moves a layout to the top level. `folder` without `position` appends; `position` without `folder` repositions within the current parent.

A folder's name cannot contain "/", which separates the folders of a `folder` path. A create, a rename or a copy that would give a folder such a name -- by its `newName`, or by the name a copy takes (`A/B Copy`) -- is `invalid_name`, and nothing is written. A folder FileMaker Pro named that way keeps its name, and a path still reaches it (see `folder` on `read`).

A rename warns where the old name is left in text. References stored by key follow the rename; text does not, so `warnings` names each place `search` finds still spelling the old name, marks one stored but not in effect, and says to change that text to the new name. The rename is not refused. `--dry-run` warns the same way, and a rename that keeps the name, or changes only its case, warns about nothing. See `filemaker help reference search` for what every search reports and which names are held as text.
A `menuSet` name the file does not have is refused when the write applies it.
A layout with no theme is given the file's default theme by any update, with a warning, even when the update says nothing about themes; a layout that has a theme keeps it.

A folder cannot be moved (`unsupported_operation`), and `theme`, the object keys and the trigger keys are refused on one. A `folder` and `position` that restate where the folder already is are accepted, beside the other keys sent.
Addressed by `name` or `id`, exactly one. A duplicated name is `ambiguous` with the candidate ids, and `id` is the way past it.
Any write rewrites the member's whole modification record: `modified.by`, `modified.account` and `modified.timestamp`. The name in `modified.by` identifies this tool and its build, not a person.
See `filemaker help reference tags` for how a tag list is written and read, and which tags FileMaker reserves.

Every key means what it means in `addObjects`, except that a key left out leaves the setting unchanged. An entry needs `id` and at least one other key, and `bounds` takes all four numbers, as on a create.

A key that belongs to another kind is refused with the kind the `id` names, since the usual cause is a stale read; `filemaker help layout layoutObject` lists the kinds each key takes. A zero extent in `bounds` is checked against that kind too. An entry takes at most one of `url` and `urlCalculation`, and at most one of `title` and `titleCalculation`.
Entries are applied in order, so the second sees what the first did. `objectsUpdated` counts the entries applied, not the objects that ended up different.

`arrange` moves an object in its parent's stacking order: `bringToFront`, `sendToBack`, `bringForward` and `sendBackward`. The last two move one position, unlike Pro, which walks up to the next object that overlaps. An object already at the front of its parent stays there and the op still reports ok.

`parent` sets what holds the object: an `id`, or 0 for the layout's top level. Containment is stated, never inferred from coordinates, because FileMaker stores it as a link: moving an object over a tab panel with `bounds` leaves it belonging to whatever held it before, and it then draws on every panel of the control. A move whose bounds newly put an object entirely inside something it is not parented to is refused, naming what it landed on. Overlap alone is left alone.

`bounds` beside `parent` is optional. Left out, the object keeps its place on screen and its bounds are rebased against the new parent's origin; sent, they are the new parent's own coordinates and are written as sent. Either way they must fall inside the new parent, because a panel, a button bar and a popover clip their children. A group is the exception: its rectangle is the union of its contents.

A popover, a tab panel and a slide panel take no `parent`: a popover belongs to its button and a panel to its control, so move the button or the control. A button cannot become or stop being a segment this way; add a segment to the bar and remove the button. A popover button, or anything holding one, cannot be moved into its own popover or the popover of a button on it.

`action` replaces the whole step the button holds and is not merged, so a key left out takes that step's default: changing `{"stepID":1,"script":"A","parameter":"\"p\""}` to `{"stepID":1,"script":"B"}` leaves no parameter. `{"stepID":0}` removes an action. Changing `bounds`, `anchors`, `objectName`, `arrange` or `text` preserves the action, including one of the sixteen steps that cannot be written onto a button, so moving, renaming or relabelling a button built in Pro is safe. `removeObjects` deletes the action with the button.
