nodes.title: findRequests
nodes.summary: a Perform Find step's find requests: which fields, what text, include or exclude

keys.summary: whether this request narrows the find ('include') or excludes what it matches ('exclude'). Leaving it out means include
what this request searches for. `[]` is a request left blank -- FileMaker allows that, and so does this
marks this whole request as one whose stored data could not be read at all. 'reason' beside it says why. Refused on write; omit findRequests to leave it alone

seeAlso: `filemaker help reference forms` — what JSON a key's type, its requiredness and a filter's tag each take
notes: `findRequests` itself is an array of these, searched one after another and OR'd together; array position is creation order and is stored exactly as sent. `[]` means no requests.
One request holds at most one criterion per field: a second criterion on the same field and repetition is refused rather than silently overwriting the first.

A criterion names its field by 'field' or 'fieldKey' -- never both. A read sends the name wherever it can and the key only where it cannot, so a criterion carrying both is refused whether or not the two agree.

A name may itself hold `::`, so an 'Occurrence::Field' value is read at each of its `::` and names the field of the one reading whose occurrence holds a field of that name: `Invoices::Line::Total` is field `Line::Total` of `Invoices`, or field `Total` of an occurrence `Invoices::Line`. A value two readings fit is refused as `ambiguous`; send the field by its raw key instead, which is how a read reports such a field.
Requests identical to the ones the step stores are left exactly as stored, so a body written back as read, or an edit that sets another key of the step, changes nothing about them.

A new criterion has to be one FileMaker's find syntax accepts for its field's type in the file's format, or it is refused as `invalid_step_option`; one holding a variable (`$when`) is stored unchecked, as FileMaker stores it. A criterion identical to one the step already stores is written as it is, unchecked: retyping a field keeps every criterion stored on it, and the read reporting one has to write back. The step is the one the write replaces -- matched by 'uuid' and 'stepID' in a body, the addressed step in an edit, and the button's or menu item's own action -- so a step sent without its 'uuid', and every step of a create, is checked in full.

Earlier versions reported date, time and timestamp criteria in a year-first form (`2026-05-12`, `2020-01-01...2020-12-31`, `12:53:09.*`). Such a text is still accepted where FileMaker's own syntax refuses it -- a year-first date in a file that writes the month or the day first -- and is stored converted into the file's format, as it was then. Where FileMaker accepts it, it is stored as sent and means what FileMaker reads: `12:53:09.*` what it always did, but `*-05-12`, in a file that writes the month first, day 5 of any month of 2012 -- send `5/12/*` for 12 May of any year.
Criteria are in the file's own format, so a body moved to a file that writes dates or numbers another way needs its criteria rewritten for that file.

children.summary: one criterion of a find request

nodes.title: criteria
nodes.summary: one criterion of one find request: a field and the text to search it for

keys.summary: the field this criterion searches, as 'Occurrence::Field'. Refused for a summary or container field, and for a field on global storage -- a global field's criterion cannot be stored at all, because writing one would write the field's own live value instead
which repetition of a repeating field, counting from 1. 1 is the default and is never reported back. Refused beside fieldKey, which carries the repetition itself

the text to search for, exactly as FileMaker stores it: FileMaker's own find syntax (`5/12`, `==3/3/2019`, `>=//`, `1/1/2020...12/31/2020`, `12:53:09`, `1,5`) in the file's own date, time and number format. Read and written as that text, never converted, so a year-less `5/12` stays a find for 12 May of whatever year it runs in. The empty string is refused -- an empty criterion is not a searchable state

the raw `[tableKey, fieldKey]` pair of a criterion whose field no longer resolves -- the field or its occurrence deleted, or its file unreachable -- or whose 'field' would read two ways, with its repetition as an optional third element. It is how such a criterion is read back. Round-trips: send it back unchanged and the criterion survives

marks this criterion as one that could not be reported as ordinary JSON -- a criterion on a global field, where reading it would mean reading the field's own live value. 'reason' beside it says why. Refused on write; omit findRequests to leave it alone

seeAlso: `filemaker help reference forms` — what JSON a key's type, its requiredness and a filter's tag each take

nodes.title: forms
nodes.summary: what a step key's form and type mean, and what JSON each one takes

forms.writes: `true` turns the option on and `false` turns it off; `null` leaves it unset. Anything else is refused. A read reports the state either way -- `true` or `false`, never an absent key -- so a body you read carries every switch the step has and hands back the same settings it came with. The exception is a key whose line says it is read only under a choice or a switch: a read leaves it out while that is not in effect. A switch stored in a number can run the other way from the number; its line then says what `true` means, and a number sent in its place is refused

several labels at once, because the value is a bitfield rather than a choice -- a window can be a card and dim its parent and have a close button. `set` names the flags that are on, from the list on the key's own line, and is what a write acts on. `raw` is the whole stored word as hex, and it carries any bit that has no label: send it back with `set` and those bits survive an edit that only changed `set`. Send `set` alone to write exactly the flags you name and nothing else. If both are sent and they disagree about a labelled flag, neither is guessed -- the write is refused

forms.json: one of the labels from the list on the key's own line
forms.writes: The label, not the integer. A read emits the label and a write takes only the label, so the round-trip is a literal echo. The integer is refused even when it is the right integer -- the diagnostic names the label it meant -- because as long as `1` worked, a body could avoid the vocabulary entirely and never be checked against it. The labels are FileMaker's own, extracted from the serializer behind its Database Design Report
FileMaker writes this one with its label showing; that is a display difference only, and it does not change what you send
FileMaker writes this one as the step's bare subject, with no label; that is a display difference only, and it does not change what you send
stored as given, and not range-checked: the number's meaning is FileMaker's, this CLI has no list of the values it allows, and one it does not recognize is written rather than refused

types.notes: see the `bareFlag` form for how a write and a read treat it

types.holds: a string holding a FileMaker calculation
types.notes: compiled when the step is written, so a syntax error or an unresolvable field name is refused rather than stored

types.holds: a string naming an existing external data source, or an integer id -- the same id an external data source reads with. 0 means the current file
types.notes: resolved when the step is written: an unknown name is refused, but an unknown id is written as sent, with a warning. "Current File" names the current file, unless the file has a data source with that literal name, in which case it is refused as ambiguous and the id must be sent instead. On a step whose script lives there -- every step with a script key beside it -- an ODBC or Claris Studio data source is `unsupported_operation`, since it holds no scripts; so is one on Re-Login, which signs in to this file or a FileMaker data source. Open File and Close File take one. Go to Related Record's `dataSource` is this same word for a different question -- "Use external table's layouts" -- and stores nothing of its own: FileMaker takes the file from the `from` occurrence, so only that occurrence's data source is accepted, and any other is `invalid_step_option` (an ODBC one is `unsupported_operation`, since it holds no layouts). Naming it makes the step use that file's layouts, with `layout` looked up there; the current file clears the choice, and leaving it out in a body uses this file's layouts. A read reports it whenever the step uses that file's layouts, whatever its `target`, but only while `from` is in another FileMaker file -- an occurrence of a table here, or of an ODBC or Claris Studio table, leaves FileMaker no other file's layouts to use, so the choice stays as stored, the write warns, and a read lists the step in `problems`

types.holds: one of the labels from the list on the key's own line
types.notes: when this key's FORM is `enum`, only the label is accepted, the same closed vocabulary the `enum` form describes. When its form is `rawInt`, the raw number is accepted too, alongside the label -- a read reports the label where one exists for the stored number, and the bare number where it does not

types.holds: a string naming a field, written `Occurrence::Field`
types.notes: resolved against table occurrences, not base tables. A read reports {"occurrence": <name>, "fieldId": <id>} instead of the string when the field no longer exists (or {"occurrence": <id>, ...} when the occurrence is gone too), and a write accepts either shape back. A write's own occurrence name is refused if it does not resolve; an occurrence or field given by id is written as sent, with a warning, if it matches nothing

types.holds: a string: either a field, written `Occurrence::Field`, or a `$variable`
types.notes: one key that holds either kind. The field form resolves against table occurrences, not base tables, so a base-table name is refused even when a field of that name exists. A deleted field reads and writes as the same {occurrence, fieldId} object the `field` type takes; a `$variable` has no such fallback, since its name is stored as plain text rather than a resolved reference

types.holds: an array of objects, each `{name, extensions}` -- the name a calculation, the extensions the file types as typed, e.g. "jpg;png"
types.notes: FileMaker's custom file-type filter list, the New/Edit/Delete rows in this step's Specify dialog. The whole list, in order: sending it replaces what was there, `[]` removes it, and one bad entry refuses the list entire rather than storing part of it
FileMaker does not name what a given number means, so it is written as given and not range-checked

types.holds: a string naming an existing layout, or an integer id -- the same id a layout reads with
types.notes: resolved when the step is written: an unknown name is refused, and one that several layouts share is refused too -- FileMaker permits duplicate names, so such a name identifies none of them; a read reports the id instead of the name in that case, and a write must send the id too. An unknown id is written as sent, with a warning.

types.holds: a string naming an existing custom menu set, or an integer id -- the same id a custom menu set reads with
types.notes: resolved when the step is written: an unknown name is refused, and one that several custom menu sets share is refused too -- FileMaker permits duplicate names, so such a name identifies none of them; a read reports the id instead of the name in that case, and a write must send the id too. An unknown id is written as sent, with a warning.

types.holds: an array of strings, each a FileMaker path expression such as `filemac:/...` or `$variable`
types.notes: a list of alternatives, tried in order; a single string is accepted and stored as a one-entry list

types.holds: a string naming an existing privilege set, or an integer id -- the same id a privilege set reads with
types.notes: resolved when the step is written: an unknown name is refused. A read reports the id instead of the name when the stored reference names nothing. An unknown id is written as sent, with a warning.

types.holds: an integer counting from 1, or a string holding a FileMaker calculation
types.notes: which repetition of a repeating field the step is on -- `Contacts::Notes[3]`. Sent alongside the field or `$variable` it modifies; sending one with neither is refused. A 1 is never reported (FileMaker does not show `[1]` either). The string form is the calculated repetition, `Notes[$i]`, and only a step's primary reference can carry one -- on the others the value is a plain number. A 0 is FileMaker's own spelling for 'the repetition is a calculation', reported where the calculation itself is under another key

types.holds: a string naming an existing script, or an integer id -- the same id a script reads with
types.notes: resolved when the step is written: an unknown name is refused, and one that several scripts share is refused too -- FileMaker permits duplicate names, so such a name identifies none of them; a read reports the id instead of the name in that case, and a write must send the id too. An unknown id is written as sent, with a warning.

types.holds: an array of strings or integer ids, each naming an existing script
types.notes: the whole list, in the order the step keeps it, with the same replace-and-refuse rules as `tableOccurrences`. A name several scripts share is refused, for the reason a shared `script` is, and unlike `script` these resolve only in the current file

types.holds: a string naming an existing table occurrence, or an integer id -- the same id a table occurrence reads with
types.notes: resolved when the step is written: an unknown name is refused. A read reports the id instead of the name when the stored reference names nothing. An unknown id is written as sent, with a warning.

types.holds: an array of strings or integer ids, each naming an existing table occurrence
types.notes: the whole list, in the order the step keeps it -- sending it replaces what was there, and `[]` removes the list rather than storing an empty one. Every entry is resolved when the step is written and one that is unknown refuses the list entire, because a list missing an entry asks for something different rather than something smaller -- unlike the singular `tableOccurrence`, an unknown id here is refused rather than written as sent. A stored occurrence that no longer exists is left out of what a read reports
not a calculation and not parsed

notes: Each line of a step's key table is a key, then its form, then its type. The form says what JSON to send; the type says what kind of value it is -- unless the line says what the key `takes`, as Perform Script on Server with Callback's `callback` and `callbackDataSource` do: each names a member, stored as a quoted key in a calc, so there the type names only the calc's own value kind and `takes` says what the quoted name actually is.

Only an opaque step -- one the CLI cannot describe -- carries `flags`, and a write that sends one back keeps that step as it was. Every other step describes its options with named keys. Options a step has no key for, for example whether a block is collapsed in Script Workspace, are kept from the existing step when the body claims it by `uuid` and `stepID`, and take FileMaker's defaults otherwise.

A step's reference to a script, a layout or a custom menu set reads back as an id instead of a name whenever more than one member answers to that name -- FileMaker permits duplicate names for these, so such a name identifies none of them, and a body carrying it would rebind the step to whichever member the catalog answered with. A reference to a table occurrence or a privilege set, whose names FileMaker keeps unique, reads back as an id only when the stored reference names nothing. Either way, sending a shared name yourself is refused for the reason above, and sending an id that names nothing is accepted and written as sent, with a warning.

A named key decides its option. Every on/off option with a key of its own -- `withDialog`, `on`, `currentFileOnly`, `breakpoint` and the like -- and a step's `dataSource` are decided by that key, or by the step's own default when the key is left out. So editing a key in a body you read does what the key says: remove `dataSource` from a Perform Script that picks its script From list and it becomes a call to the script of that name in this file, add one and it calls into that file. By name the file is part of the name, `"<data source>::<script>"`, and a `dataSource` sent beside `scriptName` is kept for From list and calls nothing. Go to Related Record's `dataSource` is the one that decides its bit only when it is sent: no data source is stored on that step to go stale, so left out of a body, "Use external table's layouts" is off, and an `edits` change to another key keeps it -- send `dataSource` to use another file's layouts, or 0 for this file's.

A value a step keeps but does not use under its current choice is not reported -- the script a Perform Script keeps From list while it performs one By name, the window name of a Select Window on the current window, Go to Record's calculation under any `selection` but `byCalculation`. The line for each such key on its step's page says when it is read. A write that does not name it keeps it, as long as the step is the same one: an `edits` change, a `body` step that carries the `uuid` and `stepID` a read gave it, or a button's or menu item's action that keeps its `stepID`. It comes back when the choice does. A layout picked from the list is the exception: an `edits` change that moves Go to Layout, Go to List of Records, New Window or Go to Related Record from it to another target leaves what FileMaker Pro's own editor for the step leaves, unless the same patch sets the layout. Go to Layout's and Go to List of Records' target popup keeps it for a target by calculation, unused, and a write that goes back to it -- one that names no target -- brings it back. Every other switch drops it, so going back without naming the layout is `missing_field`: send `layout`. An edit that sets the target the step already has changes nothing. An `edits` `set` of one switches the step to the first choice that reads it, unless the same patch sets the choice too or the value is empty. A step sent whole that names one beside a choice that does not read it keeps its choice and stores the value as kept, and the write warns, naming the choice that would read it -- except that Go to Record/Request/Page and Go to Portal Row refuse it as `step_option_not_applicable` unless it is the calculation the step already stores. AVPlayer Play is the one step whose choice follows the value it is sent: with no `source` and no `stepValue`, its `field`, `url`, `objectName` or `objectRepetition` sets the source it belongs to. Values of two sources are refused as `step_option_not_applicable`, since the step takes one, on a new step and on a step being rewritten when none of them is for the source it stores; a step being rewritten that is sent a value of its own source keeps that source, and the other values are kept and not used. Pause/Resume Script keeps a duration switched off, so the script does not pause for it under `indefinitely`.

Configure AI Account's `endpoint` and `verifySslCertificates` are a Custom provider's options: a read reports them only while `provider` is `other`, and FileMaker verifies every other provider's certificate whatever the step stores. A step on another provider keeps the values it holds, a write that does not name them leaves them, and they come back when the provider is `other` again. An `endpoint` named beside another provider is stored as kept and the write warns, as for the other values a step keeps unused, and an `edits` `set` of it moves the provider to `other`. Naming `verifySslCertificates` `true` beside another provider is `step_option_not_applicable`, unless the step already stores it; `false` is accepted and stores false.

Save Records as Excel, Save Records as PDF and Create PDF read the settings behind their "Specify options" only while `restore` is true, so a read reports them only then and each one's line says when it is read. Naming one turns `restore` on, unless the step says `restore`: false: the setting is then kept and not used, and the write warns. A setting kept that way stays through a write that does not name it, and comes back when `restore` does; naming it again with the value it already keeps does not warn. An `edits` `set` of one into a step whose `restore` is false turns `restore` on, unless the same patch sets `restore` too.

Go to Related Record's `style` is the window it opens when it shows its records in a new window, the same word New Window's `style` is. A read reports it only for a step that does (`showInNewWindow` is on), and a write of it turns that on. A step that opens a new window and stores no `style` opens FileMaker's default Document window, and reads with none. A step whose window was turned off can still hold its `style`, unused: a read reports it nowhere; an `edits` change, a `body` step that carries the step's `uuid`, or a button's or menu item's action that keeps its `stepID` keeps it; and it is the window's again when a write turns the window on without naming one.

A field or variable keeps the repetition it is on when its step is rewritten and the write names it again. A write of the same step -- an `edits` change, or a `body` step that carries the `uuid` and `stepID` a read gave it -- that names the same field or variable at the same place and does not set its repetition (the primary reference's `repetition` key, or a secondary reference's own repetition key, such as `fieldRepetition` or `messagesRepetition`) leaves it as stored: a number, a calculation, or none. A `body` step without a `uuid` is a new step, on the repetitions the body states and 1 for the rest. An `edits` change that sets or deletes a reference takes its repetition key along with it, so another field or variable starts on 1; name the repetition key in the change to keep or change one.

A `calc` key whose stored formula this run cannot render reads back under `<key>Approximate` instead of `<key>`. Sending it back under the `Approximate` key keeps the formula already stored, and only works where the body claims the same step by its `uuid` and `stepID`. `parameters`, the positional run some steps carry, has no per-position key to rename this way, so the same case reads as `null` in `parameters` at that position and the stored text at the same position in a parallel `parametersApproximate` array -- present only when at least one position needs it, and accepted back the same way. See `filemaker help reference calculations` for how a formula is sent, the Approximate keys and contextKey, and the calc_* errors.

A few steps carry a structured payload of their own, under a step-specific key -- Sort Records' `sortOrder` is one, Print's `printOptions` is another. Sending it replaces the whole thing; leaving it out keeps what is already stored. Omitting it never clears it. A step that has one lists the key itself in its own table and offers it as a sub-item; ask for that sub-item by name for its fields.

No step key is required: a step may be written with no target and no value, and it is stored as given. Two keys that set the same option are refused, though -- only one of them could survive, so which one you meant is asked rather than guessed.

A step keeps the stamps FileMaker left on it. A step an add-on installed carries where it came from and which add-on owns it, beside its `uuid`. A write of the same step -- an `edits` change, or a `body` step that carries the `uuid` and `stepID` a read gave it -- keeps them, changed or not, as editing the step in FileMaker Pro does; a step written new, inserted, copied or given another `stepID` has none. They are not keys of the step and cannot be sent.

A step in a script carries its own `tags`, an array of tags each without the leading `#`, left out of a read when the step has none. A `body` step that carries the `uuid` and `stepID` a read gave it and sends no `tags` keeps the tags it had; one that sends `tags` replaces the list, and `[]` clears it. A step with no `uuid` starts with none and takes what it sends. The tag rules, and the marks FileMaker reserves, are the same as for a catalog member's: `filemaker help reference tags`. A button's or menu item's `action` takes no `tags`: they belong on the button or item itself.
seeAlso: `filemaker help reference forms` — the same question for a catalog's keys, which carry a type, a requiredness and, on a listing, a filter tag

chunks this format does not decode, each an object naming a four-character 'tag' and its 'data' as uppercase hex. Send back what a read gave you to keep them. how many of 'preserved' came before the decoded chunk on disk. Omit it to mean first, which is the common case

refusedInputs.reason: 'type' is a create-time decision: a folder is a Begin/End bracket pair of members, so a script cannot become one in place. Delete and recreate. A separator is a script named "-", so that direction is a rename.

semanticChecks: a `tags` entry containing a space or a `#` is refused as `invalid_field`.
notes: To change a script that exists, send an `edits` patch, not a new `body`. Read the step you mean, then send one edit naming it, alongside the script's `name` and the read's `token`: `"edits":[{"op":"set","path":"/<uuid>/value","value":"1","expect":"0"}]`. The steps around it are not sent. `body` is for authoring: the steps a script starts with, or a deliberate wholesale rewrite that re-creates every step. See `help script update edits`.
Rules for writing steps -- retired steps, data sources, calculation read-back, what a dry run does not prove -- are on `filemaker help script steps`.

A step holding options a read reports `opaque`, a whole step or a find request or criterion inside one, loses them when no `body` step claims it by its `uuid` and `stepID`; `warnings` names it by the index it was read at.
A refused update writes nothing. Under `--abort-on-error=false` the script is left as it was and a later op in the batch still finds it by its old name.

A rename warns where the old name is left in text. References stored by key follow the rename; text does not, so `warnings` names each place `search` finds still spelling the old name, marks one stored but not in effect, and says to change that text to the new name. The rename is not refused. `--dry-run` warns the same way, and a rename that keeps the name, or changes only its case, warns about nothing. See `filemaker help reference search` for what every search reports and which names are held as text.
See `filemaker help reference tags` for how a tag list is written and read, and which tags FileMaker reserves.
`folder` moves the script: without `position` it is appended inside that folder, and `folder:""` moves it to the top level. `position` alone re-orders it within the folder it is in.

A folder cannot be moved: that is `unsupported_operation`. Move its scripts instead. A `folder` and `position` that restate where a folder already is are accepted beside other keys such as `hidden` or `newName`, and nothing moves.
`result` is `{name,id,membersDuplicated}`, the id unchanged and the count 0.
seeAlso: `filemaker help reference forms` — what JSON a key's type, its requiredness and a filter's tag each take

nodes.title: script update edits

keys.summary: set, replace or insert a value at `path`; delete, move or duplicate the step there
a JSON Pointer: "/<index>" or "/<uuid>" for a step, then into it by key and list index, e.g. "/0/text" or "/0/sortOrder/fields/0"

keys.condition: requiredWhen:op=set; requiredWhen:op=replace; requiredWhen:op=insert; forbiddenWhen:op=delete; forbiddenWhen:op=move; forbiddenWhen:op=duplicate
keys.conditionWords: required when `op` is `set`; required when `op` is `replace`; required when `op` is `insert`; refused when `op` is `delete`; refused when `op` is `move`; refused when `op` is `duplicate`
keys.summary: set: the new value; replace and insert: a whole step object
what `path` holds now, matched as a subset; the patch is refused if not

keys.conditionWords: refused when `op` is `set`; refused when `op` is `replace`; refused when `op` is `insert`
keys.summary: delete, move or duplicate the whole block the step at `path` opens

keys.conditionWords: required when `op` is `move`; refused when `op` is `set`; refused when `op` is `replace`; refused when `op` is `insert`; refused when `op` is `delete`
keys.summary: move or duplicate: the step to land ahead of, as a JSON Pointer

notes: An entry takes `path` and `op`. `set` also takes `value`; `replace` and `insert` take a whole step object as `value`; `delete`, `move` and `duplicate` take none. `block` widens a delete, move or duplicate to a whole block, and `before` is where a move or duplicate lands. Anything wrong with an entry, including an unknown `op` or a key its `op` does not take, is `edit_op_invalid`.

A `path` is empty or starts with "/". Its first token is a step index or the `uuid` a read reported for that step; prefer the `uuid`, which names the step wherever it now sits and survives edits made through it. An unresolvable `uuid` is `edit_path_not_found` with the near misses from the script. The rest of the path walks into the step as a JSON Pointer does, objects by key and lists by index, so the `pointer` a `search` hit carries is a `path` a `set` takes; a key or index that is not there is `edit_path_not_found`.

Every path resolves against the body as read, and all edits apply in one pass: edit 2 cannot shift edit 3's index, and a `move` or `duplicate` names its source and `before` in those same coordinates. Two steps landing in one place apply in the order listed. The set is atomic, and block balance is checked afterwards: deleting an `If` without its `End If` is `script_unbalanced_block` and nothing is written.
Only the steps an edit names are written. Every other step stays as FileMaker stored it.

A `set` replaces a list element that exists and adds an object key that does not; it never appends. A `delete` of a list element and an `insert` whose path goes inside a step are `edit_op_invalid`, because the patch's other paths resolve against the body as read, so a list changes length only by a `set` of the whole list.

`expect` is any JSON value, matched as a subset of what `path` holds; a mismatch is `edit_expect_mismatch`, reported with the value found. Send it on every edit: the token detects the file changing since the read, not a miscounted index.

`block:true` acts on the whole block the addressed step opens, from the `If` through its `End If` with every branch and nested block between. Address the opener; `block.start` in a read gives it from any step in the block. On an `End If`, an `Else`, a disabled block step or a step with no block role it is `edit_op_invalid`. An `opaque` step inside the range loses its stored options.

A `move` puts the step at `path` ahead of the step at `before`, and a `duplicate` puts a copy there; `before` is spelled the way an insert's path is, with "/<stepCount>" for the end. A move requires `before`; a duplicate without one lands right after its source. The step itself travels or is copied, so it keeps its `uuid` through a move, and an `opaque` step keeps its stored options through both, which deleting and re-inserting cannot. Each copy's new `uuid` is in `createdStepUuids`. Refused: moving a step twice, moving or duplicating a step the same patch deletes, and a `before` naming a step the patch moves or deletes or one inside the run being moved.

Inserting or deleting a step recomputes the jump targets FileMaker stores, including on steps no edit names: branch and block links, the `End Loop` that `Exit Loop If`, `Go to Record/Request/Page` and `Go to Portal Row` escape to, and a transaction's commit line. They are not part of a step's options, so a body never carries them and nothing a caller writes sets them.
An `opaque` step can be deleted and have its `disabled` set; any other edit to it is `step_not_editable`. Its stored options survive those two edits and any edit to another step.

notes: Send the `token` from the read your `edits` or `body` came from. It is required with either and ignored without them. Folders and separators carry none.

The token covers more than the script: a projection resolves field, table occurrence, layout, script, value list, custom function and data source names, so renaming any of those makes it `stale`, as does a change to a data source's paths or adding or removing one. Read the script again and rebuild the patch.

A token is judged against the run as it stands. A create, rename or delete earlier in the same run, in a catalog the token covers, makes a token read before it `stale`. A token read inside a run already accounts for that run's writes and stays good until something it covers changes after the read.

A change a projection cannot see does not spend a token, in this run or between runs: another script's steps, a layout's objects, a value list's values and a custom function's body or parameters reach it only by name. One batch can edit a function and then the script calling it, each with the token read for it beforehand. An op refused before it wrote anything spends none.
Two tokens for the same state need not be equal. Send a token; never compare two.

notes: `position` restacks the node: 0 is the front. `result.position` is where it ended up, not what was asked for. A person clicking a node in FileMaker Pro rewrites this order, so a position read from a file someone has worked in reflects their last click.

nodes.title: tableOccurrence update table
notes: Give `table` for a table in this file, or `DataSource::Table` for one in another file, such as `Inventory::Widgets`. The other file must be openable: its path resolves, the account and password this file opened with exist there, and its File Access permits this file. When it cannot be opened the answer is `tableOccurrence_unavailable`, naming which of the three it was; `dataSource` with `tableId` opens nothing.

A data source's name and a table's may each hold `::`, so the value is read at each `::`: `Inventory::Old::Widgets` is table `Old::Widgets` of `Inventory`, or table `Widgets` of `Inventory::Old`. The reading whose data source is registered and whose file holds the table is used. Two readings that both fit are `ambiguous`, naming each table with its id for `dataSource` and `tableId`. A value no reading names is the whole name of a table in this file, unless a data source it names cannot be opened, which is `tableOccurrence_unavailable`.

A value that names nothing is `table_not_found` where a registered source's file lacks the table, and otherwise `externalDataSource_not_found`, with up to three close registered names as suggestions. `create:externalDataSource` registers a reference. A data source with no table half (`Inventory`, `Inventory::`) is `unsupported_operation`; a missing name before the `::` (`::Widgets`) or an unknown data source before a final `::` (`Nope::`) is `externalDataSource_not_found`.

Two files made with `--create` cannot open each other until the referenced file authorizes this one: run `create:authorization` against it with `path` naming this file, or `update:fileOptions` with `requireAuthorization` `none` against it, which loosens the requirement for every referrer.

notes: The id is in the other file's numbering and is not checked, because this form is for a file that cannot be opened. Read it from that file first with `read:table`: a wrong id creates an occurrence that reads back `resolved:false` and dangles when FileMaker opens the graph. The qualified `table` form avoids this. Every file numbers tables from 129, so a lower id is `invalid_field`: it is almost certainly a field id.

nodes.title: theme
nodes.summary: The style sets layouts wear, each a stylesheet plus the metadata that stylesheet cannot hold
notes: A theme is named by `name`, its internal name or display name, or by `id`. A name that matches two themes is refused as `ambiguous` and lists their ids; an id always resolves. The spellings are tried in order: internal name, id, display name. The first two match exactly; the display name ignores letter case.

A theme's stylesheet (`css`), color palette (`colorPalette`) and style names (`namedStyleNames`) are three separate payloads. Each replaces itself whole and touches neither of the others, so a round trip of `css` alone loses the other two. Read `filemaker help reference themeCss` before writing `css`.

Every layout always has a theme. So `delete:theme` refuses a theme in use, an empty `css` is refused, and a new theme is always derived (`create:theme`, `duplicate:theme`), never blank. Which theme a layout wears is set on the layout (`theme` on `create:layout` and `update:layout`).

Exactly one theme is the file's default (`isDefault` on a read). `update:theme` with `"default":true` moves it; `"default":false` is refused (`invalid_field`), since a file always has one. `create:layout` and `create:theme` naming no theme or `base` use the theme most of the file's layouts wear, which may not be the default.

Write ops return `{id, name, displayName, group}` for the theme they made or changed (the copy for `duplicate`, the removed theme for `delete`), plus `warnings` when there are any. A new theme gets the id `com.filemaker.theme.custom.<uuid>` and the group "custom", and is always custom.

notes: Absent, `base` is the theme most of the file's layouts wear, which can differ from the one `read:theme` marks `isDefault`. Name it when it matters which you get.

A name that matches none of the file's themes but matches a FileMaker built-in is added to the file first and then derived from, so `"base":"Minimalist"` works in a file that never had it. The file's own themes are matched first, an internal name exactly; built-ins after, by internal name or shipped name in any letter case. A name that is neither is `theme_not_found`, and the refusal lists what this machine can add.

"Apex Blue" can always be added. FileMaker Pro's other built-ins are read from the newest installed FileMaker Pro that is not newer than this tool's FileMaker engine, so without one "Minimalist" is refused `theme_not_found`.

The compatibility theme ("Classic") and the built-ins FileMaker Pro no longer offers (`isDeprecated` on a read) are refused as `theme_unavailable`. A file that already holds one can derive from it by any of its names.

A built-in the file already holds is reused, never added twice. If the file holds two copies, its internal name is `ambiguous`: name the display name only one shows, or an id in decimal such as `"base":"1"`.

An added built-in keeps the name it ships with. If one of the file's themes already displays that name, the two share a display name (`ambiguous` from then on) and the result carries a warning naming the other. `theme` on `create:layout` and `update:layout` adds built-ins the same way.

Images ride inside the text as `-fm-image-data(name;data:image/png;base64,...)`. The form that names an image by its place in the file (`LibraryReference, id=...`) is refused (`invalid_css`). An image new to the file is stored when the batch commits.

Send `fieldId` in place of `field` only for an occurrence whose file cannot be opened. An id is not checked, so prefer the name. A read gives the id only when the name will not serve, so a read can be sent back.

notes: The reference is stored by key, so renaming the target in its file does not break it.

A data source's name and a list's name may each hold `::`. For `Inventory::Old::Colors` the CLI tries each split and uses the one whose data source is registered and whose file holds the list. If two fit, the answer is `ambiguous`, naming each list with the `dataSource` and `valueListId` to send instead.
A read gives `dataSource` and `valueListId` in place of a qualified name when the name would read two ways.

notes: A line feed, leading or trailing spaces and non-ASCII text are stored as sent.
`[""]` reads back as `[]`, because an empty list and a list of one empty value are stored the same way.

notes: A variable has no catalog, so `notFound` means the file was read and nothing used it, and there are never `candidates`. `coverage` still lists what could not be read, such as a variable whose name is computed.
